nodes.name: NF Pretreatment
nodes.procedure: Commercial nickel foam (NF) was ultrasonically cleaned in a water/hydrochloric acid (v/v, 3:1) mixture for 15 min, followed by an additional 15 min ultrasonic treatment in deionized water to remove impurities.
nodes.source_text: Commercial nickel foam (NF) was ultrasonically cleaned in a water/hydrochloric acid (v/v, 3:1) mixture for 15 min, followed by an additional 15 min ultrasonic treatment in deionized water

nodes.name: NiFe-Ce LDH Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: A mixture of 20 mmol of urea and 8.0 mmol of NH4F was added to 60 mL of deionized water under continuous stirring. Subsequently, 2.0 mmol of Ce(NO3)3·6H2O and 2.0 mmol of Fe(NO3)3·9H2O were added sequentially until a homogeneous solution formed. Pretreated nickel foam (2 cm×4 cm×1 cm) was fully immersed in the solution and transferred to a hydrothermal reactor. The reaction was conducted at 120°C for 6 h. After natural cooling, the Ni foam loaded with NiFe-Ce LDH was removed, washed thoroughly with deionized water and ethanol, and dried at 80°C for later use.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns match α-NiFe-LDH (JCPDS #40-0215) with (003) peak shifted -0.23° to lower angle and sharpened FWHM indicating lattice expansion and enhanced stacking order.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) results indicate that the diffraction peaks of the material are well-matched with α-NiFe-LDH (JCPDS #40-0215) (Figure 1b)... the introduction of Ce atoms causes a shift of the (003) diffraction peak to a lower angle compared to Ni-Fe LDH (shifted by -0.23°), indicating a lattice expansion in NiFe-Ce LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman bands at 458 cm⁻¹ (E_g Niᴵᴵ-O bending), 526 cm⁻¹ (A_{1g} stretching of brucite-like LDH), 295 cm⁻¹ (O-H); 520-530 cm⁻¹ peak blue-shifted 4.5 cm⁻¹ in NiFe-Ce LDH; no CeO₂ peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Two prominent bands at 458 and 526 cm⁻¹ corresponding to the E_g bending mode of Niᴵᴵ-O and the A_{1g} stretching mode of the Brucite-like LDH structure... the peak in the 520-530 cm⁻¹ range in NiFe-Ce LDH exhibits a certain blue shift (approximately 4.5 cm⁻¹).
Inductively coupled plasma (ICP) analysis confirmed the atomic ratio of Ni:Fe:Ce to be 55:37:8 (Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM confirms nanosheet thickness of approximately 4-5 nm for NiFe-Ce LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) measurements confirmed that the nanosheet thickness was approximately 4-5 nm (Figure 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms ultrathin nanostructure of NiFe-Ce LDH closely associated with nickel foam substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images confirmed the ultrathin nanostructure of NiFe-Ce LDH and its close association with the nickel foam substrate (Figure S9).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice spacings of 0.213 nm and 0.244 nm corresponding to (101) and (105) planes of α-NiFe-LDH with lattice expansion vs Ni-Fe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) images reveal lattice spacings of 0.213 and 0.244 nm for NiFe-Ce LDH (Figure 1e), corresponding to the (101) and (105) planes of α-NiFe-LDH, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM confirms atomically dispersed Ce within NiFe-Ce LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) analysis confirms the existence of atomically dispersed Ce within NiFe-Ce LDH (Figure 1f).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping confirms uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, and Ce elements in NiFe-Ce LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) mapping confirmed the uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, and Ce elements in the NiFe-Ce LDH (Figure 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p: Ni²⁺ (855.9/873.5 eV), Ni³⁺ (857.8/876.2 eV), Ni³⁺/Ni²⁺ ratio 0.36 (vs 0.25 Ni-Fe LDH, +0.2 eV shift); Fe 2p: Fe²⁺ (710.5/723.3 eV), Fe³⁺ (713.6/726.4 eV), -0.3 eV shift vs Ni-Fe LDH; O 1s shows oxygen vacancies facilitating LOM.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni 2p spectrum revealed peaks at 855.9 and 873.5 eV, attributed to Ni²⁺, and at 857.8 and 876.2 eV, corresponding to Ni³⁺... the Ni³⁺/Ni²⁺ ratio increased from 0.25 to 0.36... For the Fe 2p orbitals... peaks for Fe²⁺ (710.5 and 723.3 eV) and Fe³⁺ (713.6 and 726.4 eV)... the Fe 2p binding energy negatively shifted by 0.3 eV... The oxygen vacancy content at 530.8 eV followed the order: Ni-Fe LDH > NiFe-Ce LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge: absorption edge shifts higher indicating Ni²⁺ᶟ oxidation state increase; Fe K-edge: confirms Fe oxidation state reduction; Ce L₃-edge: primarily Ce³⁺ signal at 5726.1 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni K-edge XANES spectrum (Figure 2c) revealed that the absorption edge of NiFe-Ce LDH shifted to higher energies compared to Ni-Fe LDH... The Fe K-edge XANES spectrum confirmed a slight reduction in the oxidation state of Fe... The Ce L₃-edge XANES spectrum (Figure S12) displayed... Ni-Ce LDH and NiFe-Ce LDH primarily showed a strong Ce³⁺ signal at 5726.1 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS: Ni-O 1.66 Å (vs 1.63 Å Ni-Fe LDH), Fe-O 1.50 Å (vs 1.46 Å); WT-EXAFS confirms Ce-O-Ni/Fe bonds; no Ce-Ce bonds indicating isolated Ce atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transform EXAFS (FT-EXAFS) analysis revealed that the Ni-O bond length in NiFe-Ce LDH was 1.66 Å compared with 1.63 Å in Ni-Fe LDH (Figure 2e). Similarly, the Fe-O bond length increased from 1.46 to 1.50 Å in NiFe-Ce LDH... Wavelet transform EXAFS (WT-EXAFS) confirmed the formation of Ce-O-Ni/Fe bonds.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows Niᴵᴵ-OH at 458 cm⁻¹, Niᴵᴵ-O at 531 cm⁻¹ at OCP; Niᴵᴵᴵ-O peaks at 474/553 cm⁻¹ at higher potentials; new OO* peak 1000-1100 cm⁻¹ indicating LOM pathway.
nodes.evidence_snippet: At open circle potential (OCP), two Raman peaks corresponding to Niᴵᴵ-OH (458 cm⁻¹) and Niᴵᴵ-O (531 cm⁻¹)... the emergence of the Niᴵᴵᴵ-O peaks at 474 and 553 cm⁻¹... a new Raman peak between 1000 and 1100 cm⁻¹ was observed exclusively for NiFe-Ce LDH, which can be attributed to the OO* intermediate characteristic of the LOM pathway.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ ATR-SEIRAS shows *OOH at 1170 cm⁻¹ (AEM) for Ni-Fe LDH; NiFe-Ce LDH shows additional OO* at 1125 cm⁻¹ confirming hybrid AEM+LOM pathways.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the case of Ni-Fe LDH, an absorption peak at 1170 cm⁻¹ corresponding to the stretching vibration of *OOH... for NiFe-Ce LDH, an additional potential-dependent peak at 1125 cm⁻¹, assignable to the stretching vibration of O-O* species, was observed, indicating the coexistence of both AEM and LOM pathways.

nodes.characterization_summary: DEMS with ¹⁸O labeling shows ³⁴O₂/³⁶O₂ ratio >36% for NiFe-Ce LDH (vs 8% Ni-Fe LDH) confirming lattice oxygen participation in LOM.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the NiFe-Ce LDH catalyst exhibits a ³⁴O₂/³⁶O₂ ratio exceeding 36% in the heavy-oxygen water system, compared to 51% for Ni-Ce LDH and 8% for Ni-Fe LDH, demonstrating the Ce doping-induced lattice oxygen involve reaction.
